prompt: What is the difference in shape between a Pub/Sub message and a Cloud Tasks task?
hint: "This happened" against "do this".

choices.text: A message is retried and a task is not
choices.why: Both are retried.

choices.text: A task is stored on disk and a message only in memory
choices.why: Both are durable in the real services.

choices.text: A message is news for any subscriber; a task is work for one handler
choices.why: Right. A task is addressed and rate-limited.

choices.text: A message can carry a body and a task cannot
choices.why: A task carries headers and a body.

prompt: Match each queue setting to the decision it holds.
hint: How fast, how persistently.

pairs.right: How many tasks start each second
How many are in flight at once
How many tries before giving up
The first wait before a retry

right_distractors: Which region the handler lives in

prompt: The mail provider accepts five messages a second. Why set max_dispatches_per_second to 5 and not 20?
hint: What does the provider do with the other fifteen?

choices.text: Fifteen of every twenty would be refused
choices.why: Right. The downstream limit sets the rate.

choices.text: A higher rate is billed per dispatch
choices.why: The rate itself costs nothing; the refusals cost retries.

choices.text: Cloud Tasks caps every queue at 5 a second
choices.why: Queues allow far more; the provider is the limit.

choices.text: A lower rate makes each email arrive sooner
choices.why: It makes the queue drain more slowly.

prompt: What completes a task?
hint: An HTTP answer.

choices.text: The handler deleting it from the queue
choices.why: The handler never touches the queue.

choices.text: Any answer at all, even a 503
choices.why: A non-2xx answer is a failure.

choices.text: The dispatch deadline passing
choices.why: That is a failure too.

choices.text: A 2xx answer from the handler
choices.why: Right. Anything else waits and is tried again.

prompt: Within a queue, each task has a ___ that is unique, which the handler can use to recognise a duplicate.
hint: The mailer stored it in a table.

prompt: The same task reached the mailer twice. What did the second call send?
hint: The table held its name.

choices.text: A second confirmation, marked as a retry
choices.why: The terminal showed one confirmation.

choices.text: Nothing, and it still answered 200
choices.why: Right. Success stops the retries, and the table stopped the duplicate.

choices.text: Nothing, with a 409 so the queue would drop it
choices.why: It answered 200; a non-2xx would be retried.

choices.text: A 503, because the provider was down
choices.why: That was order 1043, not 1042.

prompt: Why does the mailer answer 200 to a task it has already done, rather than an error?
hint: What would the queue do with an error?

choices.text: Errors are billed and successes are free
choices.why: Billing is not the reason.

choices.text: An error would delete the queue
choices.why: An error only marks the attempt failed.

choices.text: The queue would retry finished work
choices.why: Right. The work is done, so success is the true answer.

choices.text: Cloud Tasks ignores the status code
choices.why: The status is exactly what it reads.

prompt: X-CloudTasks-TaskRetryCount was 1 on the second delivery of order 1043. Which attempt number did the mailer print?
hint: Retries are counted from zero.

prompt: The mailer checks the table, sends, then records the task. What failure can still send an email twice?
hint: Look at the gap between two lines.

choices.text: A crash between sending and the insert
choices.why: Right. The retry finds no record and sends again.

choices.text: Two different tasks for two orders
choices.why: Different orders should get different emails.

choices.text: A 400 for a request with no task name
choices.why: That sends nothing.

choices.text: The provider answering slowly
choices.why: Slowness alone does not duplicate.

prompt: Deployed, what should the mailer check instead of the X-CloudTasks-TaskName header to refuse strangers?
hint: Anybody can type a header.

choices.text: The caller's IP address
choices.why: Google's addresses are shared and change.

choices.text: A password in the request body
choices.why: A shared secret in every task is a secret in every log.

choices.text: The X-CloudTasks-QueueName header as well
choices.why: Another header is just as easy to type.

choices.text: The identity token the queue attaches
choices.why: Right. It proves who sent the request.

prompt: With min_backoff 10s, max_backoff 300s and max_doublings 3, how long does the fourth retry wait, in seconds?
A queue holds 1,800 tasks and dispatches at most 6 a second. How many seconds does it take to drain, at best?
hint: Tasks divided by rate.

prompt: Why does the sixth retry wait 240 seconds and not 320?
hint: After three doublings the wait stops doubling.

choices.text: 320 is above max_backoff
choices.why: 320 would be capped at 300, not 240.

choices.text: After max_doublings it grows by a fixed 80 seconds
choices.why: Right. 80, 160, 240, then the ceiling.

choices.text: Cloud Tasks halves the wait after five retries to clear the backlog
choices.why: No such halving.

choices.text: The program rounds to the nearest minute
choices.why: It does no rounding.

prompt: The mail provider's outages last about ten minutes, and the queue gives up 150 seconds after a first attempt. What is the honest fix?
hint: The queue must outlast the outage.

choices.text: A higher max_dispatches_per_second
choices.why: Faster dispatching fails faster.

choices.text: Answering 200 during outages
choices.why: Those emails would be lost as if sent.

choices.text: More attempts or a longer max_backoff
choices.why: Right. The retries must span longer than the outage.

choices.text: A lower min_backoff, so retries start sooner
choices.why: That shortens the span further.

prompt: A task names an order that has been deleted. What should the handler answer?
hint: Will time fix it?

choices.text: A 2xx, after logging why
choices.why: Right. Keep non-2xx for failures time can fix.

choices.text: 503, so the queue keeps trying
choices.why: Every attempt will fail the same way.

choices.text: 500, so the error is visible
choices.why: A 500 is retried like a 503.

choices.text: No answer, letting the deadline pass
choices.why: That is a failure, and is retried.

prompt: The setting that limits how many requests are in flight at once is max_concurrent____.
hint: The other brake ends in per_second.

prompt: In cron, what does 10 3 * * * mean?
hint: Minute first, then hour.

choices.text: 03:10 on the tenth of every month
choices.why: The third field, day of the month, is *.

choices.text: 10:03 every day
choices.why: Minute comes first.

choices.text: Every 10 minutes for 3 hours
choices.why: That would be */10 in the minute field.

choices.text: 03:10 every day
choices.why: Right. Minute 10 of hour 3, every day.

prompt: The nightly job is created without time_zone. When does it run in São Paulo?
hint: Scheduler reads it in UTC then.

choices.text: 03:10, because the region is southamerica-east1
choices.why: The region does not set the time zone.

choices.text: 00:10, since São Paulo is three hours behind UTC
choices.why: Right. Name the zone, and the schedule means what it says.

choices.text: 06:10, three hours after UTC
choices.why: São Paulo is behind UTC, not ahead.

choices.text: It does not run until a zone is set
choices.why: It runs, in UTC.

prompt: The shop has 7 Scheduler jobs on one billing account. With 3 free and 0.10 USD per job per 31 days, what do they cost per 31 days?
hint: Only the jobs past the free three.

prompt: A job runs every minute and another once a month. How do their Scheduler prices compare?
hint: The unit is the job.

choices.text: The first costs 43,200 times more
choices.why: Runs are not billed.

choices.text: The monthly one is free
choices.why: Free jobs are the first three, whatever their frequency.

choices.text: They cost the same
choices.why: Right. Ten cents per job per 31 days, however often it fires.

choices.text: The first is capped at one dollar
choices.why: There is no per-run price to cap.

prompt: Order the nightly report from the clock to the last store's report.
hint: Scheduler decides when, the queue how fast.
items: A handler creates one task per store
The queue dispatches them at its rate
Each store's report is built, retried on its own if it fails

prompt: Which belong in the queue rather than in the handler's code? Choose all that apply.
hint: The three decisions a queue owns.

choices.text: How many tasks start each second
choices.why: Right; a rate limit.

choices.text: How long to wait before a retry
choices.why: Right; the retry config.

choices.text: Whether a task was already done
choices.why: Only the handler can know that.

choices.text: Whether a failure is worth retrying
choices.why: The handler decides with its answer.

prompt: A sale brings 1,000 orders in a minute. Without a queue, the mailer would call the provider 1,000 times in that minute. What does the emails queue change for the provider?
hint: Five a second.

choices.text: A steady five a second for about 200 seconds
choices.why: Right. The queue absorbs the burst.

choices.text: Nothing, the queue forwards the burst unchanged
choices.why: The rate limit is exactly what it changes.

choices.text: It sends them all, then retries the refusals
choices.why: The queue never sends faster than its rate.

choices.text: It drops all but five orders a second
choices.why: Nothing is dropped; tasks wait their turn.
